description: The pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media outlets contributing to a specific political narrative analysis. It is segmented into 18 distinct slices, each labeled with a media source and its corresponding percentage value. The largest segment, colored dark blue, represents Breitbart at 14%. The next largest, gray, is labeled “Other” at 14%, indicating a collective category of smaller or unspecified outlets. Drudge Report and The Daily Caller each account for 8%, shown in orange and green respectively. NPR and Vox are both at 6%, depicted in purple and brown. The Guardian and BBC each hold 5%, in pink and dark gray. RT, Daily Kos, National Review, Daily Mail, Red State, and Fox News each represent 3%, shown in various colors including cyan, teal, lime, magenta, red, and maroon. Shareblue and PoliticusUSA are each at 3% as well, colored in lavender and salmon. The chart includes percentage labels inside each slice and a legend is implied by the direct labeling, with no slices exploded or emphasized beyond their proportional size. The segments appear roughly ordered by size in a clockwise direction starting from the top, though not strictly descending.
